To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified immunogenic T cell epitopes in COVID 19 patients.

SARS CoV specific T cell responses were identified in a proportion of COVID recovered subjects, and that these responses were mapped to 33 T cell epitopes, 28 from S protein and five from N protein, which may be used to design a multi epitope based COVID vaccine.
we identified immunodominant T cell epitopes in SARS CoV2 structural proteins and that the identified epitopes can induce SARS CoV specific memory T cell responses, but not potent responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of SARS Co V 2 specific T epitopes, and the characterization of the magnitude of T cell responses in COVID 19 subjects, providing a basis for the design of effective T cell based vaccines.
the identification of SARS Co V 2 specific memory CD4 and CD8 T cell epitopes in COVID 19 patients.
the development of a multi epitope peptide based SARS CoV specific vaccine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SARS CoV specific CD4 and CD8 T cell responses are induced in some, but by no means all COVID 19 recovered individuals, and these T cell responses correlate with neutralizing antibody responses.
our data provide a foundation for the development of effective COVID 19 vaccines and/or therapeutics, and for the rational design and evaluation of candidate COVID 19 vaccines in clinical trials.
the SARS CoV specific T cell epitopes are identified and the T cell response is correlated with B cell response in recovered COVID 19 patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified 33 SARS CoV2 specific memory T-cell epitopes, and that the T cell response to these epitopes is associated with neutralizing antibody responses.
SARS CoV specific T cell responses can be detected in some, but by far not all, recovered COVID 19 subjects, and these responses may contribute to protective immunity.
we identified SARS CoV2 specific T cell epitopes in COVID 19 subjects and the epitope specific T cells are correlated to neutralizing antibodies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
T cells play a role in the immune response to SARS CoV infection, and that this response may be protective.
the immune response to the SARS CoV-2 infection in recovered patients is not uniform.
T cell responses against SARS CoV2 are generated in COVID 19 exposed and recovered subjects, and these responses are likely to contribute to protective immunity.
